headline: Bitcoin fell to about $65,500 on Saturday morning, down about 14% in a week, as withdrawals from bitcoin funds and bets on a December rate hike kept pressure on crypto.

market.asOf: Read about 15:56-15:58 UTC Sat 14 Nov (22:56 Bangkok) from CoinCodex, because CoinGecko could not be opened this run. Blockchain.com showed bitcoin lower, at $65,810.54 (-4.53%), at the same time. Prices have moved since; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear, but indexes differ: CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index showed 19 out of 100 at about 15:58 UTC, while CryptoTicker reported a Saturday reading of 13 (20 on Friday).

stories.title: Bitcoin breaks Friday's low and trades near $65,500, down about 14% in a week
stories.summary: Weekend selling pushed bitcoin below Friday's low, its weakest level since mid-August. It is heading for a sixth losing week in a row, with a strong dollar, an expected Fed rate hike and turmoil in AI stocks all weighing on prices.
points: Bitcoin traded near $65,500 on Saturday morning US time after breaking below Friday's low of about $67,555, and is down about 14% over the past week, per Bitcoin Magazine.
It is on course for a sixth straight weekly decline (the record is nine, set in 2022), and is down 11% in November and 21% this year, per CoinDesk.
Traders have fully priced in a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the 8-9 December meeting, per CME FedWatch data cited by Bitcoin Magazine.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned with immediate effect on 12 November, per Nvidia's SEC filing; Bitcoin Magazine lists the AI-stock selloff that followed as one reason for crypto's drop.
Its twelve-month low is $58,566, set on 1 July 2026, per CryptoTicker.

sources.label: CoinDesk via Cryptonews: sixth weekly loss

stories.title: Bitcoin funds lose $2.35B in two weeks as BlackRock's IBIT logs 11 straight days of withdrawals
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the way many Americans hold bitcoin in a brokerage account, had a second straight week of withdrawals. When fund holders sell, the fund sells bitcoin, which removes buying support while prices fall. Ether funds are losing money too.
points: Spot bitcoin ETFs had $2.35B of net outflows over two weeks: $1.07B for 9-13 November and $1.28B the week before, per Cointelegraph via Cryptonews.
Friday saw $185.4M leave, of which BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $143.5M and Fidelity's FBTC $41.9M, per the same report.
IBIT has had outflows for 11 trading sessions in a row, since 30 October, per the same report.
Spot ether ETFs lost $70.5M in their latest session, a sixth straight day of outflows, per SoSoValue data reported by CoinCentral.

stories.title: Altcoins fall harder: XRP below $1 and ether below $1,900 as leveraged bets are wiped out
stories.summary: XRP dropped under $1 to its lowest level since November 2024, just as US XRP funds turned one year old with no new money coming in. Ether is falling faster than bitcoin, and borrowed bets on rising prices were force-closed on Friday.
points: XRP had its lowest daily low since November 2024, slipping below $1, and is down about 14% over seven days, per Bitcoin.com News.
US spot XRP ETFs have had no net inflows since 29 October and about $18.6M of net outflows in November, per Bitcoin.com News.
Ether fell below $1,900, with its one- and four-week losses bigger than bitcoin's, per The Defiant.
Between $1.3B and $1.6B of crypto futures bets were liquidated (force-closed) within 24 hours, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: Nvidia's CEO resigns days before earnings
briefs.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO and from the board on 12 November; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and results are still due 17 November, per Nvidia.

briefs.summary: The Justice Department also disrupted a social-engineering scheme called FaceStealer, linked to more than $400M of thefts, per TokenPost.
